title: The coherent discrete converse for every \texorpdfstring{$n\ge4$}{n >= 4}: regular four-edge anchors

blocks.tex:
This chapter documents the proof, checked in Lean, of the coherent discrete
converse four-vertex theorem in its original form: for every $n\ge4$,
\emph{every} positive cyclic curvature word which is constant or has a strict
four-vertex window at a positive level is realized by a simple moderate-arc
Euclidean $n$-gon with exactly those curvatures, closing up exactly and
turning through the real angle $2\pi$.  The Lean statement is
\verb|Gluck.Discrete.tabachnikovProblem2_all|
(\cref{thm:tabachnikov_all}); it proves the unchanged proposition
\cref{def:tab_problem2}.

We recall the exact data (\cref{def:tab_problem2},
\cref{def:discrete_fourvertex_pos}, \cref{def:discrete_realizes}).  A
curvature word is $\kappa\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$; edge $i$ joins vertex $i$ to
vertex $i+1$ and has full length $\ell_i$.

\textbf{The hypothesis.} $\operatorname{DiscreteFourVertexPos}(\kappa)$
says: every reading is positive, $\kappa_i>0$, \emph{and} either $\kappa$ is
constant or $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$ holds for some $c>0$.  The latter
(\cref{def:discrete_fourvertex}) asks for natural lifts
$i_1<i_2<i_3<i_4<i_1+n$ with $\kappa_{i_2},\kappa_{i_4}<c<\kappa_{i_1},
\kappa_{i_3}$.  Only these four positions are constrained.  Readings between
them are arbitrary positive numbers; in particular adjacent equal readings
(plateaus, constant runs) are allowed anywhere, and there is no bound on the
number of distinct values.  Positivity alone is \emph{not} a four-vertex
hypothesis, and a constant word has no strict window; the constant case is a
separate disjunct.

\textbf{The conclusion.} $\operatorname{RealizesR2}(\kappa)$ asks for lengths
$\ell\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$ with
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $\operatorname{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell$: every $\ell_i>0$ and
    both strict endpoint walls $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_{i-1}/2<1$ and
    $|\kappa_i|\,\ell_i/2<1$ hold at every vertex.  For positive $\kappa$
    this is the box $0<\ell_e<\operatorname{edgeCap}(\kappa)_e=
    2/\max(\kappa_e,\kappa_{e+1})$ (\cref{def:edge_cap},
    \cref{lem:moderate_arc_edge});
  \item exact complex closure $E(\kappa,\ell)=\sum_{k<n}\ell_k
    e^{i\psi_k}=0$, where the heading $\psi_k=\sum_{m\le k}\theta_m$ is the
    lifted sum of the turning angles
    $\theta_m=\arcsin(\kappa_m\ell_{m-1}/2)+\arcsin(\kappa_m\ell_m/2)$;
  \item real total turn $T(\kappa,\ell)=\sum_{i}\theta_i=2\pi$ (a real
    equation, not an equation modulo $2\pi$);
  \item the resulting polygon is simple.
\end{enumerate}

It is convenient to regroup the turn by edges: the \emph{gap} of edge $e$ is
$\operatorname{gap}_e=\arcsin(\kappa_e\ell_e/2)+\arcsin(\kappa_{e+1}\ell_e/2)$,
and $T=\sum_e\operatorname{gap}_e$, since each arcsine term of a turning
angle belongs to exactly one incident edge.

blocks.title: Four actual edges and their controller

blocks.label: def:four_active_frame
blocks.title: four actual edges
blocks.body:
A \emph{frame} of size $n$ is a strictly increasing choice of natural
  numbers $0\le e_0<e_1<e_2<e_3<n$; write $r_j=e_j\bmod n\in\ZMod n$ for the
  corresponding original edges (they are pairwise distinct).  For
  half-lengths $L\in\RR^4$ the \emph{ambient lengths} are
  \[
    \ell(L)_i=\begin{cases}2L_j,& i=r_j,\\ 0,& i\notin\{r_0,r_1,r_2,r_3\},
    \end{cases}
  \]
  a linear map $\RR^4\to\RR^{\ZMod n}$.  For a word $\kappa$ the
  \emph{literal endpoint readings} of the selected edges are
  \[
    s_j=\operatorname{start}_j=\kappa(r_j),\qquad
    t_j=\operatorname{finish}_j=\kappa(r_j+1).
  \]
  These are actual readings of the original word at actual indices; no
  reading is replaced or merged.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.finish
lean.code: def finish (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (j : Fin 4) : ℝ := κ (F.residue j + 1)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.start
lean.code: def start (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (j : Fin 4) : ℝ := κ (F.residue j)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.lengths
lean.code:
noncomputable def lengths (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) (i : ZMod n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j : Fin 4, if i = F.residue j then 2 * L j else 0

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame
lean.code:
structure Frame (n : ℕ) where
  edge : Fin 4 → ℕ
  strictMono : StrictMono edge
  lt_n : ∀ j, edge j < n

namespace Frame

variable {n : ℕ} (F : Frame n)

blocks.label: def:four_active_controller
blocks.title: the four-edge controller
blocks.body:
Put $\alpha_j=\arcsin(s_jL_j)$ and $\beta_j=\arcsin(t_jL_j)$, and define
  the grouped turns (subscripts of $\beta$ modulo four)
  \[
    \Theta_0=\beta_3+\alpha_0,\quad \Theta_1=\beta_0+\alpha_1,\quad
    \Theta_2=\beta_1+\alpha_2,\quad \Theta_3=\beta_2+\alpha_3 .
  \]
  With $u(x)=e^{ix}$ the controller is $C(L)=(C_1(L),C_2(L))\in\CC\times\RR$,
  \[
    C_1(L)=L_0+L_1u(\Theta_1)+L_2u(\Theta_1+\Theta_2)+
      L_3u(\Theta_1+\Theta_2+\Theta_3),\qquad
    C_2(L)=\Theta_0+\Theta_1+\Theta_2+\Theta_3-2\pi .
  \]
  Thus $C_1$ is the half-length closure of the four selected edges written in
  the heading gauge of edge $r_0$, and $C_2$ is the real turn defect.  The
  target $\CC\times\RR$ is three-dimensional, while there are four length
  variables: $C=0$ is three real equations in four unknowns.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.controller
lean.code:
noncomputable def controller (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) : ℂ × ℝ :=
  let θ := F.turns κ L
  ((L 0 : ℂ) + (L 1 : ℂ) * unitPhase (θ 1) +
    (L 2 : ℂ) * unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2) +
    (L 3 : ℂ) * unitPhase (θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3),
    θ 0 + θ 1 + θ 2 + θ 3 - 2 * Real.pi)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.turns
lean.code:
noncomputable def turns (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) : Fin 4 → ℝ :=
  ![F.finishArc κ L 3 + F.startArc κ L 0,
    F.finishArc κ L 0 + F.startArc κ L 1,
    F.finishArc κ L 1 + F.startArc κ L 2,
    F.finishArc κ L 2 + F.startArc κ L 3]

blocks.tex:
The block turn $\Theta_j$ is the whole turning between consecutive selected
edges: all intermediate readings are still present, but the zero lengths of
the intervening edges make their arcsine terms vanish.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_embedding
blocks.title: exact ambient embedding
blocks.body:
For every word $\kappa$ (with $n\neq0$ for the turn) and \emph{every}
  $L\in\RR^4$,
  \[
    T(\kappa,\ell(L))-2\pi=C_2(L),\qquad
    E(\kappa,\ell(L))=2\,u\bigl(\psi_{e_0}(\kappa,\ell(L))\bigr)\,C_1(L).
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.closureGap_eq_controller
lean.code:
theorem closureGap_eq_controller (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    closureGap κ (F.lengths L) =
      2 * unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge 0)) * (F.controller κ L).1 := by
  have hsum : closureGap κ (F.lengths L) =
      ∑ j : Fin 4, ((2 * L j : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge j)) := by
    unfold closureGap vertexR2
    rw [F.sum_range_selected]
    · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      change (F.lengths L (F.residue j) : ℂ) * _ = _
      rw [F.lengths_selected]
      rfl
    · intro k hk hne
      rw [F.lengths_unselected L (F.residue_ne_of_nat_ne hk hne)]
      simp
  rw [hsum]
  calc
    _ = ∑ j : Fin 4, ((2 * L j : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        (unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge 0)) *
          unitPhase (F.relativeHeading κ L j)) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j _
      rw [F.heading_selected κ L j, unitPhase_add]
    _ = _ := by
      rw [Fin.sum_univ_four]
      have hzero : unitPhase 0 = 1 := by simp [unitPhase]
      simp only [F.relativeHeading_zero, F.relativeHeading_one, F.relativeHeading_two,
        F.relativeHeading_three, hzero, mul_one, controller,
        Complex.ofReal_mul, Complex.ofReal_ofNat]
      ring

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.turningSum_eq_controller
lean.code:
theorem turningSum_eq_controller [NeZero n] (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    turningSum κ (F.lengths L) - 2 * Real.pi = (F.controller κ L).2 := by
  rw [F.turningSum_lengths, Fin.sum_univ_four]
  simp only [controller, turns, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one,
    Matrix.cons_val, Fin.isValue]
  ring

blocks.tex:
Both identities are proved on the whole slice, before imposing closure or
  full turn, so they may be differentiated.

  \emph{Turn.}  Write $T=\sum_{k<n}\operatorname{gap}_k$.  An unselected
  edge has $\ell_k=0$, so its gap is $\arcsin 0+\arcsin 0=0$; the sparse sum
  over $k<n$ therefore reduces to the four selected natural indices
  $e_j$.  At a selected edge $\ell=2L_j$, so its gap is exactly
  $\alpha_j+\beta_j$.  Hence $T=\sum_j(\alpha_j+\beta_j)=\sum_j\Theta_j$,
  the last step being a regrouping of the same eight terms.

  \emph{Headings.}  Unfolding the lifted heading gives
  \[
    \psi_k=\arcsin(\kappa_0\ell_{-1}/2)+\sum_{k'<k}\operatorname{gap}_{k'}
      +\arcsin(\kappa_k\ell_k/2).
  \]
  For a selected $e_j$, the prefix of gaps below $e_j$ contains exactly the
  selected edges $e_k$ with $k<j$ (the frame is increasing), so
  \[
    \psi_{e_j}=\psi_{e_0}+\Bigl(\sum_{k<j}(\alpha_k+\beta_k)\Bigr)+\alpha_j-\alpha_0 ,
  \]
  and the relative headings $\psi_{e_j}-\psi_{e_0}$ are $0$, $\Theta_1$,
  $\Theta_1+\Theta_2$ and $\Theta_1+\Theta_2+\Theta_3$ for $j=0,1,2,3$.

  \emph{Closure.}  In $E=\sum_{k<n}\ell_ku(\psi_k)$ the unselected terms
  vanish, leaving $\sum_j2L_j\,u(\psi_{e_j})$.  Factor
  $u(\psi_{e_j})=u(\psi_{e_0})\,u(\psi_{e_j}-\psi_{e_0})$ and insert the
  relative headings: the result is $2u(\psi_{e_0})C_1(L)$.  The factor
  $2$ is the full/half-length convention, and $u(\psi_{e_0})$ is the heading
  gauge; both are nonzero.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_native_rank
blocks.title: native derivative surjectivity on the active edges
blocks.body:
Let $\kappa>0$, $L_j>0$, $s_jL_j<1$ and $t_jL_j<1$ for all $j$, and
  $C(L)=0$.  Then $0\le\ell(L)_i<\operatorname{edgeCap}(\kappa)_i$ for
  every $i$, and for all $v\in\RR^4$
  \[
    DG(\ell(L))\,\ell(v)=\bigl(2u(\psi_{e_0})\,DC_1(L)v,\;DC_2(L)v\bigr),
  \]
  where $G(\ell)=(E(\kappa,\ell),T(\kappa,\ell)-2\pi)$ is the ambient
  length-only closure map.  Consequently, if $DC(L)\colon\RR^4\to\CC\times\RR$
  is surjective, then every $y\in\CC\times\RR$ is $DG(\ell(L))\,b$ for some
  $b$ with $b_i=0$ at every $i$ where $\ell(L)_i=0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.active_surj_of_controller_regular
lean.code:
theorem active_surj_of_controller_regular [NeZero n]
    {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hL : ∀ j, 0 < L j)
    (hbounds : ∀ i, 0 ≤ F.lengths L i ∧ F.lengths L i < edgeCap κ i)
    (hzero : F.controller κ L = 0)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L)) :
    ∀ y : ℂ × ℝ, ∃ b : ZMod n → ℝ,
      fderiv ℝ (fun ell => closureMapR3 (κ, ell)) (F.lengths L) b = y ∧
        ∀ i, F.lengths L i = 0 → b i = 0 := by
  have hd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (F.controller κ) L := by
    by_contra hn
    rw [fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt hn] at hsurj
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hsurj (0, 1)
    have := congrArg Prod.snd hv
    norm_num at this
  let g : ℂ := 2 * unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge 0))
  have hg : g ≠ 0 := mul_ne_zero (by norm_num) (Complex.exp_ne_zero _)
  intro y
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hsurj (y.1 / g, y.2)
  refine ⟨F.lengths v, ?_, F.lengths_direction_supported L v hL⟩
  rw [F.fderiv_lengths_at_controller_zero hκ hbounds hd hzero, hv]
  change (g * (y.1 / g), y.2) = y
  rw [mul_div_cancel₀ _ hg]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.lengths_nonneg_lt_edgeCap
lean.code:
theorem lengths_nonneg_lt_edgeCap (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (L : Fin 4 → ℝ)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hL : ∀ j, 0 < L j)
    (hstart : ∀ j, F.start κ j * L j < 1)
    (hfinish : ∀ j, F.finish κ j * L j < 1) :
    ∀ i, 0 ≤ F.lengths L i ∧ F.lengths L i < edgeCap κ i := by
  intro i
  by_cases hi : ∃ j, i = F.residue j
  · obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := hi
    rw [F.lengths_selected]
    refine ⟨(mul_pos (by norm_num) (hL j)).le, ?_⟩
    have hm : 0 < max (κ (F.residue j)) (κ (F.residue j + 1)) :=
      lt_of_lt_of_le (hκ _) (le_max_left _ _)
    rw [edgeCap, lt_div_iff₀ hm]
    have hs := hstart j
    have hf := hfinish j
    change κ (F.residue j) * L j < 1 at hs
    change κ (F.residue j + 1) * L j < 1 at hf
    rcases le_total (κ (F.residue j)) (κ (F.residue j + 1)) with hh | hh
    · rw [max_eq_right hh]
      nlinarith
    · rw [max_eq_left hh]
      nlinarith
  · have hoff : ∀ j, i ≠ F.residue j := fun j he => hi ⟨j, he⟩
    rw [F.lengths_unselected L hoff]
    exact ⟨le_rfl, (edgeCap_pos (hκ _) (hκ _)).1⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.fderiv_lengths_at_controller_zero
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_lengths_at_controller_zero [NeZero n]
    {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i)
    (hbounds : ∀ i, 0 ≤ F.lengths L i ∧ F.lengths L i < edgeCap κ i)
    (hd : DifferentiableAt ℝ (F.controller κ) L)
    (hzero : F.controller κ L = 0) (v : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun ell => closureMapR3 (κ, ell)) (F.lengths L) (F.lengths v) =
      (2 * unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths L) (F.edge 0)) *
        (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L v).1,
        (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L v).2) := by
  let g : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → ℂ := fun X =>
    2 * unitPhase (heading κ (F.lengths X) (F.edge 0))
  have hw := strict_arc_walls_of_nonneg_lt_edgeCap hκ hbounds
  have hheading := contDiffAt_heading_lengths (F.edge 0)
    (fun j _ => hw (j : ZMod n))
  have hheading' : DifferentiableAt ℝ
      (fun X : Fin 4 → ℝ => heading κ (F.lengths X) (F.edge 0)) L := by
    exact (hheading.differentiableAt one_ne_zero).comp L F.lengthsCLM.differentiableAt
  have hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g L := by
    dsimp [g, unitPhase]
    fun_prop
  have hprod := (hg.hasFDerivAt.mul hd.hasFDerivAt.fst).prodMk hd.hasFDerivAt.snd
  have hfun : (fun X : Fin 4 → ℝ => (g X * (F.controller κ X).1,
      (F.controller κ X).2)) = (fun X => closureMapR3 (κ, F.lengths X)) := by
    funext X
    apply Prod.ext
    · exact (F.closureGap_eq_controller κ X).symm
    · exact (F.turningSum_eq_controller κ X).symm
  change HasFDerivAt (fun X : Fin 4 → ℝ =>
    (g X * (F.controller κ X).1, (F.controller κ X).2)) _ L at hprod
  rw [hfun] at hprod
  have hamb := (lengthClosureMap_hasStrictFDerivAt_of_nonneg_lt_edgeCap hκ hbounds).hasFDerivAt
  have hcomp := hamb.comp L F.lengthsCLM.hasFDerivAt
  have heq := hcomp.unique hprod
  have hv := congrArg (fun A : (Fin 4 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (ℂ × ℝ) => A v) heq
  simpa [g, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, hzero, smul_eq_mul] using hv

deps.title: the length controller is strictly differentiable at zero lengths
deps.label: thm:wc_dormant_deriv

blocks.tex:
\emph{Caps.}  At a selected edge, $\ell=2L_j<2/\max(s_j,t_j)$ is
  equivalent to $\max(s_j,t_j)L_j<1$, i.e.\ to the two strict endpoint
  bounds.  At an unselected edge $\ell=0<\operatorname{edgeCap}$ because
  $\kappa>0$.  So the hypotheses of \cref{lem:wc_dormant_walls} and
  \cref{thm:wc_dormant_deriv} hold and $G$ is strictly differentiable at
  $\ell(L)$; in particular the heading $\psi_{e_0}$ is differentiable along
  the slice.

  \emph{Derivative.}  By \cref{lem:four_active_embedding},
  $G(\ell(X))=(g(X)\,C_1(X),C_2(X))$ with
  $g(X)=2u(\psi_{e_0}(\kappa,\ell(X)))$, for all $X$.  Surjectivity of
  $DC(L)$ forces $C$ to be differentiable at $L$ (otherwise its derivative is
  zero by convention).  The product rule gives
  $D(gC_1)(L)v=(Dg(L)v)\,C_1(L)+g(L)\,DC_1(L)v$, and the first term vanishes
  because $C_1(L)=0$: at a zero, differentiating the variable heading
  rotation contributes nothing.  Since $\ell$ is linear, the chain rule and
  uniqueness of derivatives give the displayed formula.

  \emph{Active rank.}  Given $y=(y_1,y_2)$, choose $v$ with
  $DC(L)v=(y_1/g(L),y_2)$, possible because $g(L)=2u(\psi_{e_0})\ne0$, and
  set $b=\ell(v)$.  Then $DG(\ell(L))b=y$.  The correction $b$ is supported
  on the four selected edges, where $\ell(L)=2L_j>0$; hence $b_i=0$ wherever
  $\ell(L)_i=0$.  No dormant direction is used to supply rank.

blocks.title: regular four-edge anchor

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor
lean.code:
structure RegularFourAnchor {n : ℕ} (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) where
  frame : FourActiveSlots.Frame n
  halfLengths : Fin 4 → ℝ
  positive : ∀ j, 0 < halfLengths j
  start_lt : ∀ j, frame.start κ j * halfLengths j < 1
  finish_lt : ∀ j, frame.finish κ j * halfLengths j < 1
  zero : frame.controller κ halfLengths = 0
  regular : Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (frame.controller κ) halfLengths)

blocks.label: lem:regular_four_reembed
blocks.title: endpoint-preserving reembedding
blocks.body:
Let $F$ be a frame of size $m$ for a word $\mu$ and $G$ a frame of size
  $n$ for a word $\kappa$, with the same literal readings:
  $\operatorname{start}^G_\kappa=\operatorname{start}^F_\mu$ and
  $\operatorname{finish}^G_\kappa=\operatorname{finish}^F_\mu$.  Then
  $C^G_\kappa=C^F_\mu$ as functions on $\RR^4$.  Hence a regular anchor
  $(F,L)$ for $\mu$ yields the regular anchor $(G,L)$ for $\kappa$, with the
  same half-lengths.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.reembed
lean.code:
noncomputable def reembed {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (A : RegularFourAnchor μ) (G : FourActiveSlots.Frame n)
    (hstart : G.start κ = A.frame.start μ) (hfinish : G.finish κ = A.frame.finish μ) :
    RegularFourAnchor κ where
  frame := G
  halfLengths := A.halfLengths
  positive := A.positive
  start_lt := by simpa only [hstart] using A.start_lt
  finish_lt := by simpa only [hfinish] using A.finish_lt
  zero := by rw [controller_eq_of_endpoints hstart hfinish]; exact A.zero
  regular := by rw [controller_eq_of_endpoints hstart hfinish]; exact A.regular

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.controller_eq_of_endpoints
lean.code:
theorem controller_eq_of_endpoints {m n : ℕ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {F : FourActiveSlots.Frame m} {G : FourActiveSlots.Frame n}
    (hstart : G.start κ = F.start μ) (hfinish : G.finish κ = F.finish μ) :
    G.controller κ = F.controller μ := by
  funext L
  simp only [FourActiveSlots.Frame.controller, FourActiveSlots.Frame.turns,
    FourActiveSlots.Frame.startArc, FourActiveSlots.Frame.finishArc, hstart, hfinish]

blocks.tex:
The controller depends on the word and the frame only through the eight
  numbers $s_j,t_j$, which enter through $\alpha_j,\beta_j$.  Equal endpoint
  functions give literally equal turns and equal controllers, as functions.
  Therefore the same $L$ satisfies positivity, the eight strict bounds (they
  are the same inequalities), $C(L)=0$, and the derivative at $L$ is the
  same linear map, so surjectivity transfers.  The number $n-4$ and the
  values of all unselected readings are irrelevant.  This is an exact
  identification, not a limiting argument.

blocks.title: Opening an anchor: every curvature fixed

blocks.label: thm:regular_four_anchor_realizes
blocks.title: a regular anchor realizes the whole word
blocks.body:
Let $n\neq0$, let $\kappa\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$ be positive, and let
  $\kappa$ have a regular four-edge anchor.  Then
  $\operatorname{RealizesR2}(\kappa)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.realizesR2
Gluck.Discrete.FourActiveSlots.Frame.realizesR2_of_controller_regular
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_of_controller_regular [NeZero n]
    {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hL : ∀ j, 0 < L j)
    (hstart : ∀ j, F.start κ j * L j < 1)
    (hfinish : ∀ j, F.finish κ j * L j < 1)
    (hzero : F.controller κ L = 0)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (F.controller κ) L)) :
    RealizesR2 κ := by
  have hbounds := F.lengths_nonneg_lt_edgeCap κ L hκ hL hstart hfinish
  have h01 := F.strictMono (show (0 : Fin 4) < 1 by decide)
  have h12 := F.strictMono (show (1 : Fin 4) < 2 by decide)
  have h23 := F.strictMono (show (2 : Fin 4) < 3 by decide)
  have h3n := F.lt_n 3
  have hn : 3 ≤ n := by omega
  have hambzero : closureMapR3 (κ, F.lengths L) = 0 := by
    unfold closureMapR3
    rw [F.closureGap_eq_controller, F.turningSum_eq_controller, hzero]
    simp
  exact realizesR2_of_regular_dormant_anchor_of_active_surj hn hκ hbounds hambzero
    (F.active_surj_of_controller_regular hκ hL hbounds hzero hsurj)

deps.label: cor:wc_dormant_active_surj

deps.title: native derivative surjectivity on the active edges
deps.label: lem:four_active_native_rank

blocks.tex:
Let $\ell^0=\ell(L)$.  By \cref{lem:four_active_native_rank},
  $0\le\ell^0<\operatorname{edgeCap}$ coordinatewise.  By
  \cref{lem:four_active_embedding} and $C(L)=0$, both $E(\kappa,\ell^0)=0$
  and $T(\kappa,\ell^0)=2\pi$: the ambient map $G$ vanishes at $\ell^0$.
  The frame has four distinct natural indices below $n$, so $n\ge4\ge3$.
  By \cref{lem:four_active_native_rank} every target of $DG(\ell^0)$ is
  reached by a correction vanishing on the collapsed coordinates
  $Z=\{i:\ell^0_i=0\}$.  This is the hypothesis of
  \cref{cor:wc_dormant_active_surj}, which gives $\operatorname{RealizesR2}$.

  For the reader we unwind that corollary.  Let $d_i=1$ for $i\in Z$ and
  $d_i=0$ otherwise.  Choose $b$ vanishing on $Z$ with
  $DG(\ell^0)b=-DG(\ell^0)d$.  Then $v=d+b$ lies in $\ker DG(\ell^0)$ and
  $v_i=1>0$ at every dormant coordinate: it points strictly into every
  collapsed face $\{\ell_i\ge0\}$.  Since $G$ is strictly differentiable with
  surjective derivative (\cref{thm:wc_dormant_deriv}), the purification
  theorem behind \cref{thm:wc_dormant_opens} provides a curve $\gamma$ in
  the length space alone --- the word $\kappa$ is never changed --- with
  $G(\gamma(\tau))=0$ and $\gamma(\tau)$ strictly inside all $2n$ slacks
  $\ell_i>0$, $\operatorname{edgeCap}_i-\ell_i>0$ for small $\tau>0$.  The
  upper slacks were already strict at $\ell^0$ and stay strict; the active
  edges were already positive; the dormant ones become positive along $v$.
  So $\ell=\gamma(\tau)$ is strictly moderate, closes exactly and has real
  total turn $2\pi$.  With $\kappa>0$ every turning angle is positive, and
  the collar realization lemma \cref{lem:collar_realizes_of_mem}, via the
  convexity theorem \cref{thm:convex_simple}, gives simplicity.

  If $n=4$ the frame is all four edges, $Z=\varnothing$, $d=0$, and the
  anchor itself is already a strictly moderate closed configuration; the same
  argument applies with a vacuous inward condition.  The opening parameter
  $\tau$ depends on the particular word; no radius uniform in $\kappa$ is
  claimed or needed.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_dfv_collapse
blocks.title: DFV survives a monotone periodic collapse
blocks.body:
Let $r\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be monotone with $r(i+n)=r(i)+m$ and
  $\mu(r(i))=\kappa(i)$ for all $i$.  If $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$
  then $\operatorname{DFV}(\mu;c)$.  Moreover any DFV word has length at
  least $4$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.DFV.four_le_period
lean.code:
theorem DFV.four_le_period {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) : 4 ≤ n := by
  obtain ⟨i₁, i₂, i₃, i₄, h12, h23, h34, h41, _⟩ := hdfv
  omega

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.DFV.of_monotone_periodic_collapse
lean.code:
theorem DFV.of_monotone_periodic_collapse
    {n m : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {μ : ZMod m → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    {r : ℕ → ℕ} (hr : Monotone r)
    (hperiod : ∀ i, r (i + n) = r i + m)
    (hreading : ∀ i, μ (r i : ZMod m) = κ (i : ZMod n))
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) : DFV μ c := by
  obtain ⟨i₁, i₂, i₃, i₄, h12, h23, h34, h41, h1, h2, h3, h4⟩ := hdfv
  have hm1 : c < μ (r i₁ : ZMod m) := by rwa [hreading]
  have hm2 : μ (r i₂ : ZMod m) < c := by rwa [hreading]
  have hm3 : c < μ (r i₃ : ZMod m) := by rwa [hreading]
  have hm4 : μ (r i₄ : ZMod m) < c := by rwa [hreading]
  have hr12 : r i₁ < r i₂ := by
    have hle := hr h12.le
    by_contra hnot
    have he : r i₁ = r i₂ := by omega
    rw [he] at hm1
    linarith
  have hr23 : r i₂ < r i₃ := by
    have hle := hr h23.le
    by_contra hnot
    have he : r i₂ = r i₃ := by omega
    rw [he] at hm2
    linarith
  have hr34 : r i₃ < r i₄ := by
    have hle := hr h34.le
    by_contra hnot
    have he : r i₃ = r i₄ := by omega
    rw [he] at hm3
    linarith
  have hr41 : r i₄ < r i₁ + m := by
    have hle : r i₄ ≤ r i₁ + m := by
      simpa [hperiod] using hr h41.le
    by_contra hnot
    have he : r i₄ = r i₁ + m := by omega
    rw [he] at hm4
    simp only [Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_self, add_zero] at hm4
    linarith
  exact ⟨r i₁, r i₂, r i₃, r i₄, hr12, hr23, hr34, hr41, hm1, hm2, hm3, hm4⟩

blocks.tex:
Push the four window witnesses forward by $r$.  Monotonicity gives
  $r(i_1)\le r(i_2)\le r(i_3)\le r(i_4)\le r(i_1)+m$.  No two consecutive
  images can coincide: their readings are $\mu(r(i_k))=\kappa(i_k)$, which
  lie strictly on opposite sides of $c$.  The same holds across the period,
  since $\mu(r(i_1)+m)=\mu(r(i_1))>c>\mu(r(i_4))$.  So all inequalities are
  strict and the images are a window at the same level.  Four strictly
  increasing naturals below $i_1+n$ force $n\ge4$.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_erase_restore
blocks.title: erase a repeated reading and restore the frame
blocks.body:
Let $w\colon\ZMod(m+1)\to\RR$ with $m\ne0$ and $w_a=w_{a+1}$ for some
  $0\le a\le m$.  Let $\operatorname{skip}_a(j)=j$ for $j<a$ and $j+1$
  otherwise, and let $w'\colon\ZMod m\to\RR$, $w'_j=w_{\operatorname{skip}_a(j)}$
  (delete entry $a$).  Then $w'$ is positive when $w$ is, and
  $\operatorname{DFV}(w;c)\Rightarrow\operatorname{DFV}(w';c)$.  Every
  frame $e_0<\dots<e_3<m$ of $w'$ gives the frame
  $\operatorname{skip}_a(e_0)<\dots<\operatorname{skip}_a(e_3)<m+1$ of $w$
  with identical start and finish functions; hence every regular anchor of
  $w'$ reembeds as a regular anchor of $w$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.restoreFrame
lean.code:
def restoreFrame {m : ℕ} (F : FourActiveSlots.Frame m) (a : Fin (m + 1)) :
    FourActiveSlots.Frame (m + 1) where
  edge := fun j => skip a.val (F.edge j)
  strictMono := (skip_strictMono a.val).comp F.strictMono
  lt_n := fun j => skip_lt (F.lt_n j)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.eraseWord_dfv
lean.code:
theorem eraseWord_dfv {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] {κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (a : Fin (m + 1))
    (hdup : κ (a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) = κ ((a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) + 1))
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) : DFV (eraseWord κ a) c :=
  hdfv.of_monotone_periodic_collapse (collapse_mono m a.val)
    (collapse_add_period m a.val) (eraseWord_collapse a hdup)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.restoreFrame_finish
lean.code:
theorem restoreFrame_finish {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (F : FourActiveSlots.Frame m)
    {κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ} (a : Fin (m + 1))
    (hdup : κ (a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) = κ ((a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) + 1)) :
    (restoreFrame F a).finish κ = F.finish (eraseWord κ a) := by
  funext j
  exact (eraseWord_finish a hdup (F.lt_n j)).symm

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.restoreAnchor
lean.code:
noncomputable def restoreAnchor {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] {κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ}
    (a : Fin (m + 1))
    (hdup : κ (a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) = κ ((a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) + 1))
    (A : RegularFourAnchor (eraseWord κ a)) : RegularFourAnchor κ :=
  A.reembed (restoreFrame A.frame a) (restoreFrame_start A.frame κ a)
    (restoreFrame_finish A.frame a hdup)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.eraseWord
lean.code:
def eraseWord {m : ℕ} (κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ) (a : Fin (m + 1)) :
    ZMod m → ℝ := fun i => κ (skip a.val i.val : ZMod (m + 1))

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.restoreFrame_start
lean.code:
theorem restoreFrame_start {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] (F : FourActiveSlots.Frame m)
    (κ : ZMod (m + 1) → ℝ) (a : Fin (m + 1)) :
    (restoreFrame F a).start κ = F.start (eraseWord κ a) := by
  funext j
  simp [FourActiveSlots.Frame.start, FourActiveSlots.Frame.residue,
    restoreFrame, eraseWord, ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt (F.lt_n j)]

blocks.tex:
Let $\operatorname{merge}_a(j)=j$ for $j\le a$ and $j-1$ for $j>a$, and
  extend periodically:
  $\rho(i)=\lfloor i/(m+1)\rfloor m+\operatorname{merge}_a(i\bmod(m+1))$.
  Then $\rho$ is monotone, $\rho(i+m+1)=\rho(i)+m$, and
  $w'(\rho(i))=w(i)$: away from $a$ this is the definition of deletion, and
  at $a$ it is the hypothesis $w_a=w_{a+1}$ (for $a=m$ it reads
  $w_m=w_0$, the cyclic successor).  \Cref{lem:four_active_dfv_collapse}
  transfers the window.  Start readings agree by definition,
  $w(\operatorname{skip}_a e_j)=w'(e_j)$.  For finish readings,
  $\rho(\operatorname{skip}_a(e_j)+1)=e_j+1$, so
  $w(\operatorname{skip}_a(e_j)+1)=w'(\rho(\operatorname{skip}_a(e_j)+1))
  =w'(e_j+1)$; this includes the wrap $e_j=m-1$.  Since $\operatorname{skip}_a$
  is strictly increasing and maps $[0,m)$ into $[0,m+1)$, the restored frame
  is a frame.  Now apply \cref{lem:regular_four_reembed}.

blocks.label: thm:four_active_restore_runs
blocks.title: finite restoration of constant runs
blocks.body:
Assume the \emph{producer statement}: for every $m$ and every
  $\mu\colon\ZMod m\to\RR$ with $4\le m$, $\mu>0$, $\operatorname{DFV}(\mu;c)$
  and $\mu_i\ne\mu_{i+1}$ for all $i$, $\mu$ has a regular four-edge anchor.
  Then every positive word $\kappa$ with $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$ has a
  regular four-edge anchor.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.ConstantRun.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_adjacent_unequal_producer
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_adjacent_unequal_producer
    (hbase : ∀ (m : ℕ) (μ : ZMod m → ℝ) (c : ℝ),
      4 ≤ m → (∀ i, 0 < μ i) → DFV μ c →
      (∀ i, μ i ≠ μ (i + 1)) → Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor μ))
    {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hdfv : DFV κ c) : Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  classical
  suffices hall : ∀ (k : ℕ) (w : ZMod k → ℝ) (c : ℝ),
      (∀ i, 0 < w i) → DFV w c → Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor w) by
    exact hall n κ c hκ hdfv
  intro k
  induction k using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | h k ih =>
    intro w c hw hd
    by_cases hne : ∀ i, w i ≠ w (i + 1)
    · exact hbase k w c hd.four_le_period hw hd hne
    · push Not at hne
      obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hne
      have hk := hd.four_le_period
      cases k with
      | zero => omega
      | succ m =>
        have hm : 0 < m := by omega
        let : NeZero m := ⟨by omega⟩
        let a : Fin (m + 1) := ⟨i.val, ZMod.val_lt i⟩
        have hdup : w (a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) = w ((a.val : ZMod (m + 1)) + 1) := by
          simpa only [a, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val] using hi
        have hd' := eraseWord_dfv a hdup hd
        obtain ⟨A⟩ := ih m (by omega) (eraseWord w a) c (eraseWord_positive hw a) hd'
        exact ⟨restoreAnchor a hdup A⟩

blocks.tex:
Strong induction on the length $k$, for all positive DFV words of that
  length.  If the word is adjacent-unequal, apply the producer; its size
  hypothesis $k\ge4$ is supplied by \cref{lem:four_active_dfv_collapse}.
  Otherwise some $w_i=w_{i+1}$.  Since $k\ge4$, write $k=m+1$ with $m\ge3$,
  delete entry $i$ as in \cref{lem:four_active_erase_restore}: the shorter
  word is positive and DFV at the same level, so it has an anchor by the
  induction hypothesis, and the lemma restores it to $w$.  The producer
  premise remains explicit in this theorem; it is discharged in
  \cref{thm:four_active_anchor_dfv}.

This section states the producer and explains its global case partition.
The first-transition producer, with its physical roots and native rank, is
proved in full in \cref{chap:discrete_native_first_pair}.  The
repeated-maximum (equal-pure) and negative-corner producers, with their
roots, incident rank and algebraic exclusion, are proved in full in
\cref{chap:discrete_native_repeated_negative}.  The mountain selection and
the transport of anchors under scaling, cyclic shift and reflection are
proved in full in \cref{chap:discrete_mountain_anchor_transport}; this
section records their interface statements.

\textbf{Normalization and transport.}  If $\kappa>0$ has a regular anchor
then so does $s\kappa$ for $s>0$ (same frame, half-lengths $L/s$;
\cref{lem:mt_anchor_scale}), so do all cyclic shifts $i\mapsto\kappa(i+a)$
(the frame is re-sorted, and when an edge crosses the origin the four slots
are rotated; \cref{thm:mt_cyclic_anchor}), and so does the reflection
$i\mapsto\kappa(-i)$ (slots reversed and start/finish swapped;
\cref{thm:mt_reflected_anchor}); in each case the zero and the derivative
surjectivity are transported as well.  For $\kappa>0$ and an index $q$ put
$\operatorname{normalizedAt}(\kappa,q)_i=\kappa_{i+q}/\kappa_q$
(\cref{def:mt_normalized}), which has value $1$ at $0$.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_transport
blocks.title: anchors transport under scaling, rotation and reflection
blocks.body:
Let $\kappa>0$.  A regular anchor of $\operatorname{normalizedAt}(\kappa,q)$
  gives one of $\kappa$; and $\kappa\circ(-)$ has a regular anchor iff
  $\kappa$ has.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.nonempty_comp_neg_iff
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_comp_neg_iff (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (-i))) ↔ Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨A⟩
    exact ⟨of_comp_neg hκ A⟩
  · rintro ⟨A⟩
    exact ⟨A.comp_neg hκ⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_normalizedAt
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_normalizedAt
    {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {q : ZMod n}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i)
    (hA : Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor (normalizedAt κ q))) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  obtain ⟨A⟩ := hA
  have B := A.scale (hκ q)
  have B' : RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (i + q)) := by
    convert B using 1
    funext i
    dsimp only [Gluck.Discrete.normalizedAt]
    field_simp [(hκ q).ne']
  exact ⟨RegularFourAnchor.of_comp_add q hκ B'⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.scale
lean.code:
noncomputable def scale (A : RegularFourAnchor κ) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) :
    RegularFourAnchor (fun i => s * κ i) where
  frame := A.frame
  halfLengths := s⁻¹ • A.halfLengths
  positive j := mul_pos (inv_pos.mpr hs) (A.positive j)
  start_lt := by
    intro j
    have hproduct : A.frame.start (fun i => s * κ i) j * (s⁻¹ • A.halfLengths) j =
        A.frame.start κ j * A.halfLengths j := by
      simp [Frame.start, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, hs.ne', mul_assoc, mul_left_comm]
    rw [hproduct]
    exact A.start_lt j
  finish_lt := by
    intro j
    have hproduct : A.frame.finish (fun i => s * κ i) j * (s⁻¹ • A.halfLengths) j =
        A.frame.finish κ j * A.halfLengths j := by
      simp [Frame.finish, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, hs.ne', mul_assoc, mul_left_comm]
    rw [hproduct]
    exact A.finish_lt j
  zero := by
    rw [A.frame.controller_scale κ hs.ne']
    simp [hs.ne', A.zero]
  regular := by
    intro y
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := A.regular ((s : ℂ) * y.1, y.2)
    refine ⟨s⁻¹ • v, ?_⟩
    rw [A.frame.fderiv_controller_scale hs.ne' A.differentiableAt_controller]
    simp [hs.ne', hv]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.RegularFourAnchor.of_comp_add
lean.code:
noncomputable def of_comp_add (a : ZMod n) (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i)
    (A : RegularFourAnchor (fun i => κ (i + a))) : RegularFourAnchor κ := by
  have B := A.comp_add (fun i => hκ _) (-a)
  simpa only [neg_add_cancel_right] using B

blocks.tex:
\emph{Scaling.}  \Cref{lem:mt_anchor_scale}: the exact identity
  $C_{s\kappa}(L)=\bigl(s^{-1}Z_\kappa(sL),\,\tau_\kappa(sL)\bigr)$
  (\cref{lem:mt_scale_identity}) holds for all $L$, the eight endpoint
  products are unchanged at $L/s$, and the derivative is the old one
  composed with invertible input and output scalings
  (\cref{lem:mt_scale_deriv}).

  \emph{Shifts.}  \Cref{thm:mt_cyclic_anchor}: a one-step shift either
  lowers all four edges (\cref{lem:mt_frame_shift}(1), endpoint readings
  unchanged, \cref{lem:regular_four_reembed}) or moves edge $0$ to $n-1$
  and rotates the slots (\cref{lem:mt_frame_shift}(2)).  In the latter case
  the rotated controller is
  $\bigl(u(-\Theta_1)[Z+L_0(u(\tau)-1)],\tau\bigr)$ off the zero set
  (\cref{lem:mt_frame_identities}); at a zero its derivative is
  $(z,t)\mapsto(u(-\Theta_1)(z+iL_0t),t)$, with the lifted-turn term
  $iL_0t$ surviving (\cref{thm:mt_deriv_transport}), and the explicit
  preimage transfers surjectivity (\cref{thm:mt_reembed}).

  \emph{Reflection.}  \Cref{thm:mt_reflected_anchor}: the reversed frame
  swaps start and finish readings (\cref{lem:mt_frame_reverse}); the
  reversed controller is
  $\bigl(u(\Theta_1+\Theta_2+\Theta_3)\,\overline{Z},\,\tau\bigr)$, whose
  derivative at a zero is
  $(z,t)\mapsto(u(\Theta_1+\Theta_2+\Theta_3)\overline{z},t)$, again
  invertible.

  \emph{Normalization.}  \Cref{thm:mt_restore_normalization}: scale the
  anchor of $\operatorname{normalizedAt}(\kappa,q)$ by $\kappa_q$ to obtain
  one of $i\mapsto\kappa_{i+q}$, then undo the shift by $q$.

\textbf{The first-pair flag.}  Put
$\sigma(h,l)=\sqrt{(1-l^2)/(h^2-l^2)}$ and
\[
  \Phi(p,q,h,l)=\arcsin p+\arcsin\bigl(q\,\sigma(h,l)\bigr)
    -\arcsin\sigma(h,l)-\tfrac{\pi}{2}
\]
(\cref{def:nfp_flag}).  If $p<1$ and $q\le1$ then $\Phi(p,q,h,l)<0$
(\cref{lem:nfp_flag_negative}); the consequences of $\Phi\ge0$ are
\cref{lem:nfp_flag_bounds}.

\textbf{Physical native producers.}  All three producers work on the
normalized four-edge model with starts $(1,t,q,l)$ and finishes $(p,q,h,1)$:
the first edge starts at the normalized peak $1$, the second and third
edges meet at a high reading $q$, and the last edge returns to $1$.  In this
case the frame controller is literally the native controller $N$ of
\cref{def:nfp_native_model}, and a zero $L$ of it satisfying the physical
conditions (positivity of the four half-lengths and the eight strict
endpoint bounds for these readings) with surjective derivative packages into
a regular anchor (\cref{lem:nfp_to_anchor}).  For $0<p,l<1$, $0<t<q$ and
$1<q<h$ every such physical zero has surjective derivative
(\cref{thm:nfp_native_rank}).
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Equal-pure (repeated maximum), $q=1$}: for
    $p,t,h,l\in(0,1)$, a physical zero exists on an interior equal-pure
    orthogonal core (\cref{thm:nrn_repeated_zero}: uniform residual signs on
    an inner rectangle and the Poincar\'e--Miranda theorem), and at every
    physical zero the second pure turn is nonacute, which gives rank three
    (\cref{thm:nrn_equal_pure_rank}).  Both are proved in
    \cref{chap:discrete_native_repeated_negative}.
  \item \emph{First transition}, $0<p<1$, $0<t<q$, $0<l<1$, $1<q<h$,
    $\Phi(p,q,h,l)\ge0>\Phi(p,t,q,l)$: the producer
    (\cref{thm:nfp_transition}) splits into the \emph{pure} case $t\le p$
    (\cref{thm:nfp_pure_anchor}: a boundary strip and an inward
    intermediate-value argument, using only the nonnegative flag) and the
    \emph{ordered} case $p<t$ (\cref{thm:nfp_ordered_anchor}: a crossed
    winding argument on the original residual rectangle, which also uses the
    predecessor comparison $\Phi(p,t,q,l)<0$).  Both are proved in
    \cref{chap:discrete_native_first_pair}.
  \item \emph{Negative corners}, $0<p,l<1$, $0<t<q$, $0<h<q$, $1<q$,
    $\Phi(p,t,q,l)<0$ and $\Phi(l,h,q,p)<0$: a physical zero on the
    orthogonal core exists (\cref{thm:nrn_negative_zero}: a clamped-square
    fixed point with signs only at boundary zeros, where the two negative
    flags are the corner values).  Its rank is proved by splitting on the
    second pure turn: if $\arcsin(qL_1)+\arcsin(qL_2)\ge\pi/2$ (nonacute,
    equality included) a direct incident rank argument applies
    (\cref{thm:nrn_nonacute_rank}); in the acute chamber rank loss forces
    two actual derivative minors to vanish and produces a solution of an
    explicit polynomial system (\cref{lem:nrn_rank_loss_packet}), which is
    proved to have none by exact elimination and a sign argument
    (\cref{thm:nrn_packet_false}).  Together: \cref{thm:nrn_negative_regular}.
\end{itemize}
These are proved Lean theorems, not assumptions.  The first-transition
proof, including its predecessor and equality boundaries, is written out in
\cref{chap:discrete_native_first_pair}; the equal-pure and negative-corner
proofs, including the literal frame selection
(\cref{thm:nrn_repeated_anchor}, \cref{thm:nrn_negative_anchor}), are
written out in \cref{chap:discrete_native_repeated_negative}.

blocks.label: def:four_active_secondary_peak
blocks.title: highest secondary peak
blocks.body:
Given a marked index $H$ of a word $\kappa$, an index $q$ is a
  \emph{highest secondary peak} if $q\ne H$, $q$ is a strict local maximum
  ($\kappa_{q-1}<\kappa_q>\kappa_{q+1}$), and $\kappa_i\le\kappa_q$ for every
  strict local maximum $i\ne H$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak
lean.code:
structure HighestSecondaryPeak (κ : ZMod n → ℝ) (H q : ZMod n) : Prop where
  ne_global : q ≠ H
  is_peak : IsStrictLocalMax κ q
  maximal : ∀ i, i ≠ H → IsStrictLocalMax κ i → κ i ≤ κ q

blocks.label: lem:four_active_mountain
blocks.title: selection and the single mountain
blocks.body:
Let $\kappa$ be adjacent-unequal with $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$.  For
  every $H$ a highest secondary peak $q$ exists.  If moreover
  $\kappa_q<\kappa_H$ then there are $2\le a\le(H-q)\le b\le n-2$ (natural
  offsets from $q$) such that, for $j<n$, $\kappa_{q+j}>\kappa_q$ iff
  $a\le j\le b$, and $j\mapsto\kappa_{q+j}$ is strictly increasing on
  $[a,H-q]$ and strictly decreasing on $[H-q,b]$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.exists_highestSecondaryPeak
lean.code:
theorem exists_highestSecondaryPeak {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (hdfv : DFV κ c) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) (H : ZMod n) :
    ∃ q, HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨i, j, hij, hi, hj⟩ := hdfv.exists_two_strictLocalMax hne
  let s := Finset.univ.filter (fun i : ZMod n => i ≠ H ∧ IsStrictLocalMax κ i)
  have hs : s.Nonempty := by
    by_cases hiH : i = H
    · exact ⟨j, by simp [s, hj, show j ≠ H by intro e; exact hij (hiH.trans e.symm)]⟩
    · exact ⟨i, by simp [s, hiH, hi]⟩
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hmax⟩ := s.exists_max_image κ hs
  have hqm : q ≠ H ∧ IsStrictLocalMax κ q := by simpa [s] using hq
  exact ⟨q, hqm.1, hqm.2, fun i hiH hi => hmax i (by simp [s, hiH, hi])⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.exists_mountain
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.exists_mountain {κ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {H q : ZMod n} (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) (hH : κ q < κ H) :
    ∃ a b : ℕ, 2 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ (H - q).val ∧ (H - q).val ≤ b ∧ b + 2 ≤ n ∧
      (∀ j < n, κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)) ↔ a ≤ j ∧ j ≤ b) ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun j : ℕ => κ (q + (j : ZMod n))) (Icc a (H - q).val) ∧
      StrictAntiOn (fun j : ℕ => κ (q + (j : ZMod n))) (Icc (H - q).val b) := by
  classical
  let s := (Finset.range n).filter (fun j : ℕ => κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)))
  have hmem : ∀ j, j ∈ s ↔ j < n ∧ κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)) := by
    intro j; simp [s]
  have hHmem : (H - q).val ∈ s := by
    rw [hmem]
    refine ⟨ZMod.val_lt _, ?_⟩
    simpa [ZMod.natCast_zmod_val] using hH
  have hs : s.Nonempty := ⟨_, hHmem⟩
  let a := s.min' hs
  let b := s.max' hs
  have ha := (hmem a).mp (s.min'_mem hs)
  have hb := (hmem b).mp (s.max'_mem hs)
  have haH : a ≤ (H - q).val := s.min'_le _ hHmem
  have hHb : (H - q).val ≤ b := s.le_max' _ hHmem
  have ha2 : 2 ≤ a := by
    by_contra h
    have ha01 : a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by omega
    rcases ha01 with ha0 | ha1
    · simpa [ha0] using ha.2
    · have hh : κ q < κ (q + 1) := by simpa [ha1] using ha.2
      exact (not_lt_of_gt hq.is_peak.2) hh
  have hb2 : b + 2 ≤ n := by
    by_contra h
    have hbn : b = n - 1 := by omega
    have hidx : q + (b : ZMod n) = q - 1 := by
      rw [hbn, Nat.cast_sub (by omega : 1 ≤ n), ZMod.natCast_self]
      simp [sub_eq_add_neg]
    have hh : κ q < κ (q - 1) := by simpa [hidx] using hb.2
    exact (not_lt_of_gt hq.is_peak.1) hh
  have hinterval : ∀ j < n, κ q < κ (q + (j : ZMod n)) ↔ a ≤ j ∧ j ≤ b := by
    intro j hj
    constructor
    · intro hh
      have hjmem := (hmem j).mpr ⟨hj, hh⟩
      exact ⟨s.min'_le _ hjmem, s.le_max' _ hjmem⟩
    · rintro ⟨haj, hjb⟩
      exact hq.high_interval hne ha.1 hb.1 ha.2 hb.2 haj hjb
  refine ⟨a, b, ha2, haH, hHb, hb2, hinterval, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i hi j hj hij
    rcases hi with ⟨hia, hiH⟩
    rcases hj with ⟨hja, hjH⟩
    apply hq.rising_lt hne hij hjH
    exact (hinterval i (by omega)).mpr ⟨hia, by omega⟩
  · intro i hi j hj hij
    rcases hi with ⟨hiH, hib⟩
    rcases hj with ⟨hjH, hjb⟩
    apply hq.falling_lt hne hiH hij (by omega)
    exact (hinterval j (by omega)).mpr ⟨by omega, hjb⟩

deps.title: existence of the highest secondary peak
deps.label: lem:mt_secondary_exists

blocks.tex:
Existence is \cref{lem:mt_secondary_exists}: a window in an
  adjacent-unequal word gives two distinct strict local maxima
  (\cref{thm:n6mr_two_strict_max}), so a strict local maximum other than $H$
  exists, and one of largest value is selected.  The mountain is
  \cref{thm:mt_mountain}: above level $\kappa_q$ no reading other than $H$
  is a strict local maximum, so every high reading climbs strictly to $H$
  along actual consecutive indices (\cref{lem:mt_high_path}); such paths
  cannot pass through $q$ (\cref{lem:mt_no_wrap}), so the high offsets form
  one interval (\cref{lem:mt_high_interval}), rising before and falling
  after $H$ (\cref{lem:mt_legs}); the neighbours of $q$ are lower, which
  gives $a\ge2$ and $b\le n-2$.  There is no bound on $n$ or on the number
  of distinct readings, and either leg may be trivial.

blocks.title: anchors for every adjacent-unequal DFV word
blocks.body:
Let $4\le n$, $\kappa\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$ positive with
  $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$ and $\kappa_i\ne\kappa_{i+1}$ for all $i$.
  Then $\kappa$ has a regular four-edge anchor.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_forward_terminal
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_forward_terminal
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H 0)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (hzero : κ 0 = 1) (hH : 1 < κ H)
    (hflag : 0 ≤ firstPairFlag (κ 1) (κ (H - 1)) (κ H) (κ (-1))) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  apply hq.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_rising_terminal hκ hne hzero hH
  simpa only [natPred_val_residue hq.ne_global.symm] using hflag

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_backward_terminal
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_backward_terminal
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H 0)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (hzero : κ 0 = 1) (hH : 1 < κ H)
    (hflag : 0 ≤ firstPairFlag (κ (-1)) (κ (H + 1)) (κ H) (κ 1)) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  have hq' : HighestSecondaryPeak (fun i => κ (-i)) (-H) 0 := by
    simpa using hq.comp_neg
  apply (RegularFourAnchor.nonempty_comp_neg_iff hκ).mp
  apply hq'.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_forward_terminal (fun i => hκ (-i))
    (adjacent_ne_comp_neg hne) (by simpa using hzero) (by simpa using hH)
  simpa [neg_sub, add_comm] using hflag

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_repeated_global_maximum
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_repeated_global_maximum
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H J : ZMod n}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (hmax : ∀ i, κ i ≤ κ H) (hJ : κ J = κ H) (hJH : J ≠ H) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  let μ := normalizedAt κ H
  have hμ : ∀ i, 0 < μ i := normalizedAt_pos hκ H
  have hle : ∀ i, μ i ≤ 1 := by
    intro i
    exact (div_le_one (hκ H)).mpr (hmax (i + H))
  have hμne : ∀ i, μ i ≠ μ (i + 1) := normalizedAt_adjacent_ne hne (hκ H)
  have hzero : μ 0 = 1 := by simp [μ, normalizedAt, (hκ H).ne']
  have hJ' : μ (J - H) = 1 := by simp [μ, normalizedAt, hJ, (hκ H).ne']
  apply nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_normalizedAt hκ (q := H)
  exact nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_repeated_normalized_maximum hμ hle hμne
    hzero hJ' (sub_ne_zero.mpr hJH)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor
lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H q : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H q)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (hglobal : ∀ i, i ≠ H → κ i < κ H) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  let μ := Gluck.Discrete.normalizedAt κ q
  have hq' : HighestSecondaryPeak μ (H - q) 0 := hq.normalizedAt (hκ q)
  have hμ : ∀ i, 0 < μ i := normalizedAt_pos hκ q
  have hμne : ∀ i, μ i ≠ μ (i + 1) := normalizedAt_adjacent_ne hne (hκ q)
  have hzero : μ 0 = 1 := by simp [μ, Gluck.Discrete.normalizedAt, (hκ q).ne']
  have hH : 1 < μ (H - q) := by
    simpa [μ, Gluck.Discrete.normalizedAt] using (one_lt_div (hκ q)).mpr (hglobal q hq.ne_global)
  have hglobal' : ∀ i, i ≠ H - q → μ i < μ (H - q) := by
    intro i hi
    have hneq : i + q ≠ H := by
      intro he
      exact hi (eq_sub_iff_add_eq.mpr he)
    simpa [μ, Gluck.Discrete.normalizedAt] using
      div_lt_div_of_pos_right (hglobal (i + q) hneq) (hκ q)
  apply nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_normalizedAt hκ (q := q)
  change Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor μ)
  by_cases hf : 0 ≤ firstPairFlag (μ 1) (μ ((H - q) - 1)) (μ (H - q)) (μ (-1))
  · exact hq'.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_forward_terminal hμ hμne hzero hH hf
  · by_cases hb : 0 ≤ firstPairFlag (μ (-1)) (μ ((H - q) + 1)) (μ (H - q)) (μ 1)
    · exact hq'.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_backward_terminal hμ hμne hzero hH hb
    · exact hq'.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_negative_terminals hμ hμne hzero hH
        hglobal' (lt_of_not_ge hf) (lt_of_not_ge hb)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_adjacent_unequal_dfv
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_adjacent_unequal_dfv
    {n : ℕ} {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
    (hn : 4 ≤ n) (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hdfv : DFV κ c)
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1)) : Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  classical
  let : NeZero n := ⟨by omega⟩
  obtain ⟨H, _, hmax⟩ := Finset.univ.exists_max_image κ
    (by simp : (Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod n)).Nonempty)
  have hmax' : ∀ i, κ i ≤ κ H := fun i => hmax i (Finset.mem_univ i)
  by_cases hrepeat : ∃ J, J ≠ H ∧ κ J = κ H
  · obtain ⟨J, hJH, hJ⟩ := hrepeat
    exact nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_repeated_global_maximum hκ hne hmax' hJ hJH
  · have hglobal : ∀ i, i ≠ H → κ i < κ H := by
      intro i hi
      apply lt_of_le_of_ne (hmax' i)
      intro he
      exact hrepeat ⟨i, hi, he⟩
    obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := exists_highestSecondaryPeak hdfv hne H
    exact hq.nonempty_regularFourAnchor hκ hne hglobal

blocks.tex:
Choose $H$ with $\kappa_H=\max\kappa$.

  \emph{Repeated maximum.}  Suppose $\kappa_J=\kappa_H$ for some $J\ne H$.
  Normalize at $H$: $\mu=\operatorname{normalizedAt}(\kappa,H)$ is positive
  and adjacent-unequal (\cref{lem:mt_peak_symmetry}) and has
  $\mu\le1$, $\mu_0=1=\mu_{J'}$ with $J'=J-H\neq0$.  Adjacent-unequality
  places $J'$ at natural offset $2\le J'\le n-2$, and the four readings
  $p=\mu_1$, $t=\mu_{J'-1}$, $h=\mu_{J'+1}$, $l=\mu_{-1}$ all lie in $(0,1)$.
  The frame of the edges $0,J'-1,J',n-1$ (the four edges incident to the two
  maxima) has starts $(1,t,1,l)$ and finishes $(p,1,h,1)$, and the
  equal-pure producer gives the anchor (\cref{thm:nrn_repeated_anchor}(2),
  which also proves the index separation).  Transport back by
  \cref{thm:mt_restore_normalization}.

  \emph{Unique maximum.}  Otherwise $\kappa_i<\kappa_H$ for $i\ne H$.  Take a
  highest secondary peak $q$ (\cref{lem:mt_secondary_exists}) and normalize
  at $q$: $\mu=\operatorname{normalizedAt}(\kappa,q)$ is positive and
  adjacent-unequal, $0$ is a highest secondary peak for $H'=H-q$
  (\cref{lem:mt_peak_symmetry}(4)), $\mu_0=1<\mu_{H'}$, and
  $\mu_i<\mu_{H'}$ for $i\ne H'$; its mountain is
  \cref{lem:four_active_mountain}.  Consider the forward terminal flag
  $\Phi_+=\Phi(\mu_1,\mu_{H'-1},\mu_{H'},\mu_{-1})$.
  \begin{itemize}
    \item If $\Phi_+\ge0$ (equality included): along the rising leg
      $[a,H']$, the entry $\mu_{a-1}\le1$ has negative flag, so there is a
      first $i$ with $a\le i<H'$, $\Phi(p,\mu_i,\mu_{i+1},l)\ge0$ and
      $\Phi(p,\mu_{i-1},\mu_i,l)<0$, where $p=\mu_1<1$ and $l=\mu_{-1}<1$
      (\cref{lem:nfp_rising_transition}).  Here
      $\mu_{i-1}<\mu_i<\mu_{i+1}$ and $\mu_i>1$.  The frame $0,i-1,i,n-1$
      has starts $(1,\mu_{i-1},\mu_i,l)$ and finishes $(p,\mu_i,\mu_{i+1},1)$
      (\cref{lem:nfp_frame}), and the first-transition producer gives the
      anchor (\cref{thm:nfp_rising_anchor}(3), \cref{thm:mt_forward_terminal};
      the low entry and the identification of $H'-1$ are
      \cref{lem:mt_normalized_entry}).
    \item Else, if the backward flag
      $\Phi_-=\Phi(\mu_{-1},\mu_{H'+1},\mu_{H'},\mu_1)\ge0$: apply the previous
      case to the reflected word $i\mapsto\mu_{-i}$ (the highest secondary
      peak and adjacent-unequality are reflection invariant,
      \cref{lem:mt_peak_symmetry}; the reflected forward flag is literally
      $\Phi_-$), so that \cref{thm:nfp_rising_anchor}(3) gives an anchor of
      the reflected word, and restore orientation by
      \cref{thm:mt_reflected_anchor}.  This is \cref{thm:mt_backward_terminal}.
    \item Else $\Phi_+<0$ and $\Phi_-<0$: the frame $0,H'-1,H',n-1$ of the
      edges incident to the secondary peak and to the global maximum has
      starts $(1,\mu_{H'-1},\mu_{H'},\mu_{-1})$ and finishes
      $(\mu_1,\mu_{H'},\mu_{H'+1},1)$; uniqueness of the maximum gives
      $\mu_{H'\pm1}<\mu_{H'}$, and the two negative flags are exactly the
      negative-corner hypotheses.  The negative-corner producer gives the
      anchor (\cref{thm:nrn_negative_anchor}(2)).
  \end{itemize}
  In each branch undo the normalization by \cref{thm:mt_restore_normalization}
  (the interface \cref{lem:four_active_transport}).
  The three alternatives are exhaustive for every such word.

blocks.label: lem:four_active_const
blocks.title: constant words
blocks.body:
If $n\ge3$, $c>0$ and $\kappa_i=c$ for all $i$, then
  $\operatorname{RealizesR2}(\kappa)$, by the regular $n$-gon with full edge
  length $(2/c)\sin(\pi/n)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesR2_of_const
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_of_const [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n) {k : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hk : ∀ i, k i = c) : RealizesR2 k := by
  have hfun : k = fun _ : ZMod n => c := funext hk
  rw [hfun]
  exact realizesR2_const hn hc

blocks.body:
Assume the producer statement of \cref{thm:four_active_restore_runs}.
  Then $\mathrm{TP2}(n)$ holds for every $n\ge4$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.tabachnikovProblem2_of_adjacent_unequal_regular_anchors
lean.code:
theorem tabachnikovProblem2_of_adjacent_unequal_regular_anchors
    (hproducer : ∀ (m : ℕ) (μ : ZMod m → ℝ) (c : ℝ),
      4 ≤ m → (∀ i, 0 < μ i) → DFV μ c →
      (∀ i, μ i ≠ μ (i + 1)) → Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor μ))
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (hn : 4 ≤ n) : TabachnikovProblem2 n := by
  intro κ hκ
  obtain ⟨hpositive, hconst | hdfv⟩ := hκ
  · obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hconst
    exact realizesR2_of_const (by omega) (by simpa only [hc 0] using hpositive 0) hc
  · obtain ⟨c, _, hd⟩ := hdfv
    obtain ⟨A⟩ := ConstantRun.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_adjacent_unequal_producer
      hproducer hpositive hd
    exact A.realizesR2 hpositive

blocks.tex:
Let $\operatorname{DiscreteFourVertexPos}(\kappa)$.  If $\kappa\equiv c$,
  positivity gives $c>0$ and \cref{lem:four_active_const} applies.
  Otherwise $\operatorname{DFV}(\kappa;c)$ for some $c>0$;
  \cref{thm:four_active_restore_runs} gives a regular anchor and
  \cref{thm:regular_four_anchor_realizes} realizes $\kappa$ with every
  reading unchanged.

blocks.body:
For every $n\ge4$, $\mathrm{TP2}(n)$: every positive word
  $\kappa\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$ that is constant or has a strict four-vertex
  window at a positive level is realized by a simple moderate-arc Euclidean
  polygon with exactly those curvatures, exact closure and real total turn
  $2\pi$.

    (fun _ _ _ hm hp hd ha => nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_adjacent_unequal_dfv hm hp hd ha) hn
